clue.text: Literary idiot crumbling a dry bun in boat

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the vessel word, splitting it after its third letter

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat

indicators.note: crumbling breaks the bun to pieces, so the letters of a dry bun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foolish character in a novel breaks up a stale bun aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbling' rearranges the letters of 'a dry bun', and 'in' places them inside the boat word, after its third letter. Barnaby is the simple-minded hero of Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's title character is a simple-minded youth, the idiot of that novel.

clue.text: Growth on 'ead — growth on head — giving one a bell

parts.note: growth on the head is hair; the dropped H of 'ead tells you to drop it, leaving AIR
a lock is a tress of hair growing on the head

explanation.surface: A Cockney-flavoured remark about hair growing on the head somehow leads to phoning someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving one a bell' looks like the British idiom for telephoning someone. In fact a bell is also a bubble, and an airlock is a bubble of air trapped in a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell can mean a bubble in liquid, and an airlock is a trapped bubble of air blocking a pipe.

clue.text: Country, one without love and friend

indicators.note: without tells you to take the letter for love away from the number word

parts.note: taken as the word itself
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone without love is left with only a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country lying between India and China.

clue.text: Little half of capital old city

parts.note: baby means little, as in a baby carrot

indicators.note: half of keeps just the first three of the six letters of the capital city

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK

explanation.surface: A small part of a capital city is old.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was the ancient city of Mesopotamia on the Euphrates.

clue.text: Literary lady's place reportedly in the vegetable garden

indicators.note: reportedly tells you the word is heard spoken, so it sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: Tennyson's poem The Lady of Shalott names Shalott as her home

explanation.surface: A poem's heroine is said to live among the vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's Lady of Shalott lives at Shalott, which sounds the same as the onion-like vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb grown among the produce of a kitchen garden.

clue.text: Hunt the painter, opening (not ending) with island

indicators.note: not ending tells you to drop the final letter of the word for opening

parts.note: a hole is an opening
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A hunt for a painter begins at an island.
explanation.walkthrough: William Holman Hunt was a Pre-Raphaelite painter, so the definition is his middle name, the one that comes before Hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: William Holman Hunt, the Pre-Raphaelite artist, carried this name directly before his surname.

clue.text: Model for foot, one for backside, curtains for all

parts.note: a last is the shoemaker's wooden model of a foot
one is another model, the Ford Model T, giving the letter T
rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A shoemaker's form is used for the foot and another for the behind, then it's the end for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' is slang for the end; the Last Trump sounds at the end of the world, Judgement Day, for all.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet call on Judgement Day signals the end of the world, meaning death for everyone.

clue.text: Summons to Pullman's girl, good cleaner

parts.note: oi is a call to summon someone's attention
Lyra is the heroine of Philip Pullman's His Dark Materials

explanation.surface: Calling to Philip Pullman's heroine praises her as a good cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oi, Lyra!' is how one might shout to her.
explanation.definitionFit: An oily rag is a cloth used for cleaning machinery, hence a cleaner.

clue.text: Breach caused by creative skill arising in …

indicators.note: in puts the upturned skill word inside the agreement word

parts.note: the ellipsis points to the next clue, whose answer means a convention

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means the letters read upward, so backwards

parts.note: art is creative skill

explanation.surface: A breach is caused by creative skill rising up within something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads on to the next clue, whose answer means convention. 'arising' turns ART into TRA, put into CONVENTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A contravention is a breach of a rule or law.

clue.text: Hold 1 16's 25

definitions.meaning: the title character of the Dickens novel at 1 and 16 has a pet bird, the answer at 25

explanation.definitionFit: A grip is a firm hold, and also the name of the talking bird belonging to the Dickens character.

clue.text: In vain going in one's stockinged feet?

definitions.meaning: bootless is an old word for useless, so in vain
walking without shoes on, read literally as lacking boots

explanation.definitionFit: Bootless means unavailing, so the adverb means fruitlessly; read literally it means without boots on.

clue.text: Nothing left after payment for antique fair

indicators.note: after puts the payment word first, with the other letters coming behind it

parts.note: a toll is a payment for using a road or bridge
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Once the payment is made, nothing remains for a fair selling antiques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antique' says the word is old slang; 'fair' is the meaning, pretty good, not a market.
explanation.definitionFit: Tol-lol is old slang for fairly good or passable, so an archaic word meaning fair.

clue.text: Vehicle that goes backwards on hills had a 17 28 in …

indicators.note: a vehicle that goes backwards has its letters read in reverse

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
tors are rocky hills, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A vehicle rolls backwards down hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into the next clue: Marina Lewycka's novel is titled A Short History of Tractors in Ukrainian. 'that goes backwards' turns CART into TRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The farm machines are the subject of Marina Lewycka's novel A Short History of Tractors in Ukrainian.

clue.text: … this country's weather in a translated language

parts.note: for a British paper, this country is the UK
rain is a kind of weather

indicators.note: translated changes in a into another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The British weather is described in a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukrainian is the official language of Ukraine.

clue.text: … a friend of the environment seizing me before time of treaty

indicators.note: seizing means the environmental word holds the pronoun inside it

parts.note: a Green is an environmentalist
taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: An environmentalist grabs the speaker before the treaty's time comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' puts ME into GREEN as GREE-ME-N.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement is a treaty or pact between parties.

clue.text: See 1
Annal, perhaps, of Labour politician: the man's Conservative

parts.note: Clare Short was a Labour cabinet minister
his means belonging to the man
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Labour politician's chronicle reveals that her partner is a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's two words describe an annal only loosely, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a brief year-by-year record, an example of a concise chronicle of past events.

clue.text: Garter's first word about rebellion by elusive character

indicators.note: about means the motto word goes around the rebellion letters

parts.note: the Order of the Garter's motto begins Honi soit qui mal y pense
UDI, Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence in 1965, was an act of rebellion against Britain

explanation.surface: The opening of a knightly motto concerns an uprising led by a slippery figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini, the escapologist, was famously impossible to hold captive.

clue.text: Distinguish Archer, giving him a role

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: An archer stands out by being given a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer' suggests the novelist Jeffrey Archer, but it is William Tell, who shot the apple.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell apart is to distinguish one thing from another.

clue.text: Garter, say, the French half including the Guardian

clue.text: Brazilian diplomacy read in vain to 24

parts.note: Rio, Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city
tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Brazilian diplomacy is lectured fruitlessly to a general.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Gordon Riots of 1780, the backdrop of the Dickens novel, the Riot Act was read to Lord George Gordon's mob without effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was the statute read aloud to order a crowd to disperse, which the Gordon rioters ignored.

clue.text: Magician at the wheel?

definitions.meaning: Harry ... is the boy wizard in J K Rowling's books
someone who works at a ... wheel shaping clay

explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter is a fictional wizard, and a potter shapes clay at a wheel.

clue.text: Dice carrot, say, as 2 of 8

definitions.meaning: to cube a root vegetable is to cut it into dice
two is the number that, cubed, makes eight

explanation.definitionFit: Two multiplied by itself three times is eight, and dicing a carrot cuts a root into cubes.

clue.text: Chinese general followed by the bad guys in 1 16

definitions.meaning: General Charles 'Chinese' ... earned his nickname in China

definitions.text: followed by the bad guys in 1 16
definitions.meaning: Lord George ... led the rioters of 1780 portrayed in the Dickens novel

explanation.definitionFit: Two famous bearers of the surname: the general in China and the anti-Catholic agitator of 1780.

clue.text: Bird with mosaics if not available

indicators.note: not available is abbreviated N/A, and if not tells you those two letters are missing

parts.note: Ravenna in Italy is famous for its Byzantine mosaics

explanation.surface: A bird comes with mosaics unless they cannot be had.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Setter securing home in club in the soup

indicators.note: securing means the setter's word holds everything else inside it

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: in puts the home word inside the club word

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler shelters a house within a club and ends up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble; here 'in the' only links. 'In' puts the home inside the club, and 'securing' wraps the setter around both.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup.

clue.text: Food for those who live alone

indicators.note: the food is provided by those words, sitting across the join of live and alone

explanation.surface: Something to eat for people living by themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: There is hardly an indicator; the letters run across 'live alone'. SOLE, for those who are alone, is a tempting wrong answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the meat of a calf, a kind of food.

clue.text: See 17
The beginning of beginning? Have a go at grasping this theological mystery

indicators.note: grasping means the attempt word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: to try is to have a go at

indicators.note: the beginning of keeps only the opening letters of the word for beginning

parts.note: initial means beginning, as in the initial stage

explanation.surface: Wondering what came before the start, someone attempts to understand a religious mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The beginning of beginning?' looks like a riddle about the dawn of time. It means: take the start of a word meaning beginning, and 'grasping' puts it inside the attempt word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trinity, God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit, is the central mystery of Christian theology.
